## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

(Canonical criteria — promoted from the producer-approved re-scope of 2026-11-09; they supersede the original AC1–AC6 recorded below. Original AC6 includes the `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard, which C6 relocates and updates.)

- **P1. No test lost or doubled** — suite runs the same 475 tests with identical per-file `unit`/`integration`/`e2e` membership as the `dev` baseline (unit 257 / integration 215 / e2e 3), verified by a before/after selection diff.
- **P2. Standard layout** — every `*.test.ts` lives under a top-level `tests/` tree (`tests/<area>/`, `tests/deploy/`, `tests/support/`, `tests/scripts/`); `tsconfig.json` includes `tests/**/*.ts`.
- **P3. Isolation preserved** — no Phaser/DOM file flattened into the node `unit` project; an equivalent deterministic membership guard passes.
- **P4. Aliases** — `@/*` → `src/*` resolves in `tsc`, Vite and Vitest; the classifier follows it.
- **P5. Tooling + docs** — test-skill type profiles (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) still run; comments, AGENTS.md and dev notes updated (CHANGELOG excluded — ship skill).
- **P6. Full suite passes.**

## Superseded original acceptance criteria (replaced 2026-11-09 by the P1–P6 re-scope above)

Retained for traceability only; NOT the completion gate — P1–P6 above are.

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

## Related work

- AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV — parent of the unit/integration split decision

- **P5. Tooling + docs** — test-skill type profiles (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) still run; comments, AGENTS.md and dev notes updated (CHANGELOG excluded — ship skill).

# Implement the Music System defined by the Audio Design Chapter

## Goal

Build the runtime background-music system for AI Hell against the fixed design contract captured in
`docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` (produced by **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)**).

User story: *As a player, I want a dynamic, retro-arcade soundtrack that responds to combat intensity, so
that runs feel like the relentless survival experience the game is aiming for; and as a developer I want the
music engine driven by a documented parameter/state contract, so behaviour is testable and reproducible.*

> **Scope stance:** this is **future scope, out of MVP** (GDD §8). The MVP ships baked ToneForge SFX only
> (GDD §7.3), and §7.3 remains authoritative for SFX. This item must **not** be started until the design
> chapter exists and has been reviewed, and it must **not** promote music into the MVP without an explicit
> producer decision.

## Background

- AI Hell currently has **no background music** by design: GDD §7.3 keeps music out of MVP scope, and the
  player-fire grid is deliberately quantised to a **silent internal 80 BPM beat** (AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B).
- SFX are build-time baked WAV assets rendered deterministically by ToneForge and played through Phaser's
  shared `AudioContext` (`src/audio/effects.ts`); the authoritative cue catalogue is
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`.
- The Audio Design Chapter specifies the musical identity (Phrygian Dominant combat scale, Lydian ambient
  scale, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), instrumentation palette, dynamic-mixing rules, state-driven
  transitions, parameter mapping, audio budget and accessibility requirements.

## Expected behaviour and outcomes

- A music system that plays layered/stemmed music driven by an explicit game-state parameter, with
  bar-boundary transitions, stingers, and ducking, as specified by the chapter.
- Music state follows gameplay (e.g. menu/attract, wave combat, boss, low-health tension, run end) with the
  transition rules and timings given in the chapter, and never disrupts the beat grid or the SFX mix.
- Reproducible, deterministic behaviour suitable for automated tests; no audio regressions to the shipped SFX
  pipeline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Contract traceable to the chapter:** every implemented music state, transition, stinger and mixing parameter traces to a named section of `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md`, recorded in a mapping table in the implementation docs.
- [ ] **AC2 — Musical content matches the documented identity:** the delivered cues/stems use the chapter's scales, motifs and progressions (Phrygian Dominant combat, Lydian ambient, Combat Motifs A/B, "Star Drift"), verified by an explicit audit table (motif → scale degrees → usage state).
- [ ] **AC3 — State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.
- [ ] **AC4 — Dynamic mixing implemented:** ducking, per-layer volume targets and the priority tiers behave as specified; SFX intelligibility is preserved (music ducks under key SFX cues) and is covered by tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Autoplay and accessibility compliance:** no audio before a user gesture (`AudioContext` resume discipline, GDD §7.3); the chapter's accessibility requirements (e.g. music/SFX independent volume, mute, and any reduction options) are implemented and documented.
- [ ] **AC6 — Budget met:** the shipped music respects the chapter's audio budget (memory, streaming, polyphony, layer count) on the supported targets, measured and recorded.
- [ ] **AC7 — Docs updated:** GDD §7.3 and §8 are updated to reflect the shipped music system, and `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` is marked as implemented for the sections that ship.
- [ ] **AC8 — No SFX regression:** the existing ToneForge baked-SFX pipeline and cue catalogue remain unchanged and their tests pass; any chapter §6.4 procedural SFX recipes are explicitly **not** adopted unless decisioned separately.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project build and test suite pass.**

## Constraints

- **Blocked by** the docs item **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — this item
  must not begin before `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` exists.
- Music stays **out of MVP scope** until a producer decision promotes it (GDD §7.3, §8).
- Keep the gameplay SVG/vector aesthetic and retro-arcade palette of the chapter; UK English in all docs.
- §7.3 (baked ToneForge SFX) remains authoritative for SFX; the chapter is an addendum whose §6.4 procedural
  SFX recipes are design reference only.
- Prefer reusing the existing audio plumbing (`src/audio/effects.ts`, shared `AudioContext`, manifest-driven
  playback) over introducing new runtime dependencies; any middleware adoption (the chapter's FMOD/Wwise
  guidance) is a separate decision — the web build currently has no middleware.

## Approach (indicative)

1. Confirm scope with the producer (MVP vs post-MVP) and record the decision on this item.
2. Ingest the chapter into an implementation mapping table (state → parameter → cue/stem set → transition).
3. Decide the delivery mechanism (baked stems via ToneForge + `AudioContext` playback, per the existing
   pipeline) versus a runtime synthesiser; record the trade-off before coding.
4. Implement the music state machine and mixing layer behind a single facade, mirroring the existing SFX
   façade style; add unit tests per transition and per mixing rule.
5. Add accessibility controls and the autoplay guard; verify budget and measure on target hardware.
6. Update GDD §7.3/§8 and the chapter's implemented-sections marker.

**Key Files:**
- `docs/AUDIO_DESIGN_CHAPTER.md` — the design contract (prerequisite)
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — existing SFX façade / shared `AudioContext` plumbing to reuse
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — where combat-state music parameters would be driven from
- `src/core/rules.ts` — game-rules config (including `beatBpm`) that music tempo must stay coherent with
- `src/audio/` — new music module + tests
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 and §8 updates

## Risks & assumptions

- **Overlap with the shipped silent beat grid (medium):** player fire is quantised to an internal 80 BPM beat.
  Music must be tempo-coherent with that grid or the two will fight; assume music tempo is either locked to
  `beatBpm` or documented as intentionally independent.
- **Chapter/SFX divergence (medium):** the chapter's §6.4 procedural SFX recipes differ from the shipped baked
  catalogue; §7.3 stays authoritative (AC8).
- **Middleware assumption (low):** the chapter's FMOD/Wwise guidance is forward-looking; no middleware exists in
  the web build, so it is design intent only.
- **Scope creep into MVP (medium):** music is out of MVP; promotion needs an explicit producer decision.

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — prerequisite; produces the design contract.
- discovered-from:AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W
- GDD §7.3 (SFX, authoritative for MVP), GDD §8 (Future Scope — "Background music"), and
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (SFX cue catalogue).
- Beat grid / timing context: AH-0MUAYB8EH005RJ8B (beat-aligned fire grid), AH-0MV01HNLU008S5E3 (beat-timed
  explosion accents).

Test-first item for the parent AC "Enemy counts rise with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

Add tests (in the existing wave test files, or a new `src/waves/scaledCampaign.test.ts`) that:

## Goal

**User story:** As a balance engineer, I want deterministic tests that prove the kill-time power-up supply falls with the campaign level, so the supply curve cannot regress unnoticed.

Test-first item for the parent AC "Power-up supply per enemy falls with level" (AH-0MVHT1M6O003PU7P).

Extend `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` (and the rules tests where appropriate) with tests that:

- New tests fail on pre-change HEAD (flat 0.18 roll for every level).
- Assertions are exact and seeded — no statistical/threshold flakiness.
- Coverage includes level 1 identity, level 10 endpoint, mid-run level advance, unknown-level fallback and Extra Life proportionality.
- No production code is modified by this item (tests only).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`
- `src/core/rules.test.ts`

- [ ] Boss spawn transitions to the boss state and plays the documented boss progression (E-C-D-F-E, extendable for later phases).
- [ ] Crossing into low health enters the tension state, and restoring health returns to the underlying state.
- [ ] Stingers cut in at the documented points (not bar-boundary-only) and return to the underlying music state afterwards.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid transitions and reset paths, and transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified).
- [ ] The boss and low-health states are driven by the shared combat core so PlayScene and the gyms stay in parity.

- [ ] Covers parent AC3: **State machine implemented and tested:** transitions occur only at the documented boundaries (bar boundaries unless a stinger cut-in is specified), with unit tests covering each transition in the chapter's transition matrix, including invalid/reset paths.

# Intake brief — Ring win: massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls lose state (post-MVP)

Headline: Implement the deferred Candidate D win/lose semantics — an algorithmic hangar assault resolved from stored numbers when a ring's final hex is captured, a legible defence report, and a full-campaign reset when the hangar falls.

## Problem statement

Candidate D's States section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **the last hex taken and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls**. The shipped MVP (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE, producer decision 2026-10-30 Q2 = a) deliberately narrows this: ring secured = every hex held, no assault pass, and no hangar-falls lose state — so a player can never lose the campaign. This work item ships the deferred semantics.

## Users

The single player of the Hangar War campaign. Holding the whole ring currently just opens the next checklist; this change makes the ring-end a real, legible defensive milestone and gives the campaign a true lose condition.

Example user stories:

- As a player who has captured every hex of a ring, I want the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar to be resolved and reported from the same stored numbers that decide hex defence, so the ring win feels like a victory I earned, not a checkbox.
- As a player who cannot hold the hangar, I want the campaign loss to be announced legibly and reset the campaign, so losing the hangar is a real consequence while losing a single hex battle never costs me my fleet.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1. Capturing the ring's final hex triggers an algorithmic hangar-assault resolution from stored numbers, with a report showing the numbers that produced the result.
- AC2. A repelled assault marks the ring won (the existing win state, now gated on the assault); a failed assault applies the hangar-falls consequence: a **full campaign reset** (hangar and ring wiped together). Losing a hex battle never resets the hangar.
- AC3. The resolver is a pure module exercised in the `GymHexWar` gym, with unit tests for repel, fall and boundary cases; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated if the gym surface changes.
- AC4. The attract bot traverses or skips the assault report without stalling.
- AC5. GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` record the chosen win/lose semantics; build and full suite green; all related documentation updated (including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki/docs entries).
- AC6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player can now lose the campaign only when the hangar itself falls — and when they hold the ring, they defend it in a legible, deterministic showdown instead of silently opening the next ring.

## Constraints

- **No live simulated battle** (Candidate D's algorithmic-resolution rule, attract-mode requirement): the assault is arithmetic over stored numbers, matching the existing hex defence resolver's shape.
- **Gym↔game parity** (AGENTS.md): the resolver must live in the shared core and be consumed by both the game (`PlayScene`/generation paths) and the `GymHexWar` gym; no divergent copies.
- **Determinism/replay**: the resolution must draw from the same seeded, bounded-jitter stream as the hex resolver so a replay reproduces every outcome bit-for-bit.
- **Proportion to the existing system**: reuse the `hexDefence.ts` vocabulary (`resolveDefence`/`runFrontierTick`, tuning, seeded streams) rather than inventing a parallel resolution model.

## Existing state

- The defence resolver and frontier tick (`src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`) resolve hex defence from `{defenderRating, attackingForce, aggression, seed}` with bounded seeded jitter; a secured ring has no unheld neighbour and draws no attacks — "quiet by construction", with an explicit note that the hangar assault is deferred to this item.
- Ring-win handling (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`): `isRingOpenable` (every hex held, or the capstone held for the rush line) gates `openNextRing`, which generates the next ring from authored definitions. There is no assault pass and no lose state.
- The defence report (`src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts`, `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`) renders a frontier tick record without re-deriving figures; a quiet tick publishes an explicit "no hex was attacked" line so the attract demo cannot stall.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` exercises the model/renderer surface with the deterministic control-surface stand-in (`fakeFrontierClock`).
- Docs of record: GDD §8.2 (ring-secured rule, resolver/tick numbers, defence report, measured timings) and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D (States, Minimal first slice).

## Desired change

1. **Assault trigger and resolution.** When the last hex of a ring is captured, resolve a hangar assault algorithmically from stored numbers (producer Q2 = A): defender side = **sum of held hex defender ratings**; attacker side = **a base massed force derived from the ring's numbers** (sum of ring hex aggression, or the ring aggression budget) scaled by the same `aggressionPercentPerPoint` multiplier the hex resolver uses, with the same bounded seeded jitter. Repel and fall are both determined with the full arithmetic exposed in the defence report.
2. **Win gate.** A repelled assault marks the ring won (the existing per-ring win triggered by final-hex capture, now gated on the assault) and opens the next ring as today. The rush line (capstone held, ring not fully held) is **unchanged and out of scope**: it opens the next ring exactly as today because no assault is triggered — the assault only fires when the ring's final hex is captured (AC1).
3. **Lose state (producer Q1 = B).** A failed assault = the hangar falls = **full campaign reset**: the hangar (hulls, weapons, modifiers, banked salvage/cores) and the ring hexes are wiped together, and the reset is announced in the defence report. A hex falling in the normal frontier tick never triggers this and never resets the hangar.
4. **Report.** Extend the defence report to render the assault's numbers (held-ring defender sum, massed force, aggression multiplier, jitter, assault strength, margin, outcome) and, on a fall, the reset consequence.
5. **Docs.** Record the chosen win/lose semantics in GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D States / Minimal first slice), replacing the "deferred" note.
6. **Attract/test surface.** The report must be traversable or skippable by the attract bot (no stall), and the resolver exercised in `GymHexWar` with unit tests.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts` — add hangar-assault types (`HangarAssaultInput`/`HangarAssaultResolution`-equivalent), the base massed-force derivation, and `resolveHangarAssault` reusing the seeded jitter stream; extend `FrontierTuning` if a new knob (e.g. assault mass base) is needed.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — gate ring win/loss on the assault: final-hex capture triggers assault; fall → full campaign reset payload; repel → ring won + `openNextRing`.
- `src/core/hangarWar/defenceReport.ts` / `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` — render the assault record and the reset announcement.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — payload fields for the assault record / save reset, if any (versioned additively).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` — exercise the assault surface; verify attract traversal.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — route the capture seam through the assault gate (shared core, not divergent).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8, §8.2) — record the win/lose semantics.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D States / Minimal first slice) — record the chosen semantics, remove the deferred note.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — update if the gym surface changes (AC3).

## Related work

- **AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE** — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (the MVP that deferred this item; parent context).
- **AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88** — the hex defence resolver (in scope reference).
- **AH-0MVUXCBBK004EJIP** — the defence report.
- **AH-0MVUXCC5J0028OGQ** — Hangar War documentation of record.
- **AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A** — ring-timing re-measure (related; not blocking).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MVUXCAW0001VUM6** – Capture cycle: hex deployment, boss-granted discovery and defending bot (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXCA0J0011W88** – Pure defence resolver and frontier aggression clock (completed)
- **AH-0MVXSHAS100010S0** – Rush push into the next ring is playable (AC8 gap) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvu3vnji00066ye, acceptance, actually, agents, aggression (+146 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvu3vnji00066ye, acceptance, actually, agents, aggression (+144 more)
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` — matched: 0mvu3vnji00066ye, actually, agents, aggression, algorithmic (+127 more)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** the rush line (capstone-held opens the next ring without an assault) is deliberately excluded — assault only fires on full-ring final-hex capture; any change to ring-opening semantics becomes a new work item.
- **Balance risk:** an under- or over-tuned massed-force base makes the new lose state either a formality (always repel) or a trap (always falls). Mitigate by reusing the earned defender numbers (sum of held ratings) and tuning the base from the ring's own numbers; measured ring timings (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A) can validate.
- **Reset-completeness risk:** the "full campaign reset" must cover every persisted field (hangar + ring + pending attacks + seed progression) — a partial reset is a data-integrity bug. The payload version should remain valid and a fresh campaign seed issued.
- **Attract-mode regression risk:** a new report surface must be traversed or skipped by the bot; verify with an attract test (AC4).
- **Assumption:** the assault is fully deterministic from the payload (seeded), so no wall-clock or live battle is involved.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q1: "When the hangar-falls assault fails (the lose state), what is the consequence?" — Answer (producer, reply to AH-C0MWETZ16W0086O8E): **B — full campaign reset**; "loss of a hex battle does not reset hangar, loss of the hangar does". Source: producer reply, 2026-11-13, recorded in comment AH-C0MWEUVENV000WDS8. Prior answer: none (open at intake start). Accepted: B.
- Q2: "What numbers compose the AI's massed assault force in the algorithmic resolution?" — Answer (producer): **A — reuse the ring stored numbers**: defender = sum of held hex defender ratings; attacker = base massed force from ring numbers (sum of ring hex aggression, or ring aggression budget) scaled by `aggressionPercentPerPoint` with the same bounded seeded jitter. Source: producer reply, 2026-11-13, recorded in comment AH-C0MWEUVENV000WDS8. Prior answer: none. Accepted: A.

# Post-MVP Hangar War: special missions with special rewards

## Problem statement

The Hangar War's ring is its biggest design risk: six identical hexes can read
as six chores, and nothing rewards a player with anything beyond the shipped
salvage currencies. A player should occasionally be offered a **special
mission** whose completion pays a genuinely **special reward** — a new hull
with extra hit points, not another currency drop — so the ring always has a
"what should I take, what should I risk" decision and never a pure checklist.

## Users

- **The returning ring player** — "I've ground the ring once; I want an
  occasional hex that offers something I can't just buy, so every sortie can
  surprise me with a real upgrade rather than another 40 minerals."
- **The strategist** — "I want to see the special mission's reward before I
  commit a life, so the risk of an unusual task is a choice, not a gamble."

## Scope

- A **special-mission hex** authored in the ring data (Q1 = a, producer answer
  2026-11-13): one kind of hex whose deployment is an ordinary one-level
  capture — the shipped `PlayScene` + `src/scenes/core/` path ends on the
  level's mini-boss — and whose grant on capture is the **special reward**
  instead of a currency drop.
- The **reward** is a hull with **extra hit points** (Q2 = a): a new catalogue
  entry (e.g. `hull-3`) expressible with today's `HullDefinition` /
  `HullRunStats` model (`startingLives` / `baseDefence`), granted through the
  existing `resolveHexGrant` path into `unlockedHulls`. **Upgrade bays are out
  of scope** — tracked separately as AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY (producer request).
- The **offer rotates** (Q3 = b): a seeded rotation between sorties decides
  which special hex/offer is presented, so the ring changes between
  deployments rather than being fixed at authoring time; rotations are
  deterministic for a given payload seed (the shared `createHangarWarRng`
  stream), never a UI-visible surprise rule.
- **Known-ahead intel applies**: the reward is visible in the map's detail
  panel before the player commits — no special mission is a blind box.
- Reuses the shipped deployment path and pure hangar economy; **no second run
  implementation** (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity). Everything stays under the one
  `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload (field-presence migration; no new storage key).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Authored special-mission hex.** A special-mission hex type is
  authored ring data (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` + CSV seeds),
  validated loudly by the ring validator, and completed through the shipped
  one-level deployment (mini-boss victory) — no second run implementation
  (gym↔game parity).
- **AC2 — Special reward, real and persistent.** Completing a special mission
  grants a new hull with **extra hit points** through the existing
  `resolveHexGrant`/owned-sets path; the hull has a real effect when deployed
  and persists under the `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload with field-presence
  migration (no new storage key).
- **AC3 — Seeded rotating offer (Q3 = b).** The presented special hex/offer
  rotates between sorties from the shared seeded RNG — deterministic for the
  payload seed (same seed → same rotation sequence), never ad-hoc randomness
  in a scene.
- **AC4 — Known-ahead intel.** The map's detail panel publishes the special
  mission's reward and any special framing before the player commits to the
  deployment (the tile stays a legible short label).
- **AC5 — Gym coverage and docs.** `GymHangar` (and `GymHexWar` where the map
  surfaces the offer) exercise the reward/economy/rotation behaviour with the
  same code as the game. Tests pin the reward, the rotation/gating and the
  persistence round-trip; full suite green. All related documentation (GDD
  §8.2, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments and README entries.

## Impact

Players will occasionally find a hex worth a detour that pays a hull with real
extra survivability instead of another currency drop, so the ring keeps
offering a decision — what to take, what to risk — rather than one more box to
tick.

## Constraints

- **Q1 = a:** special missions are authored ring data deployed as ordinary
  one-level captures; no second deployment/run implementation (gym↔game
  parity).
- **Q2 = a:** the first special reward is a hull with extra hit points,
  expressible in the shipped catalogue model and granted via the existing
  grant path. Upgrade-bay rewards are out of scope (AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY).
- **Q3 = b:** the offer rotates through the shared *seeded* RNG per sortie;
  deterministic for the payload seed, replayable.
- **Known ahead:** the reward is published before the player commits (existing
  known-ahead intel surface).
- **One payload:** any per-hex special-mission state lives in
  `ai_hell_hangar_war` with field-presence migration; no new storage key.
- **Validation rejects, never repairs:** malformed special-mission authored
  data fails loudly exactly as `validateRingDefinitions` / `HexRingDefinitionError`
  do today.
- **Design of record:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D post-MVP
  list and GDD §8.2; each idea judged by the anti-checklist test (adds a
  choice rather than a chore).

## Existing state (research)

- **Authored ring data:** `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` (typed table) and
  `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` (seed mirrors; parity tests
  guard drift) — `HexRingDefinition` carries `id`, `q`/`r`, `ringIndex`,
  `boss`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `grants`, `weaponHex`, `baseAggression`.
  Validation in `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`
  (`validateRingDefinitions` → `HexRingDefinitionError`), pinned by
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts`.
- **Capture/grant path:** `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — the
  four-step capture (bank salvage → grant entry → leave defender → secure
  ring); `resolveHexGrant` translates an authored `grants` id to the hangar's
  owned sets (weapons → `unlockedWeapons`, hulls → `unlockedHulls`, modifiers →
  `ownedModifiers`) via `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` + `GRANT_ALIASES`.
- **Catalogue model:** `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — `HullDefinition`
  (`baseDefence`, `upgrades`, `runStats: { startingLives, speedMultiplier }`),
  `StartingWeaponDefinition`, `ModifierDefinition`; extra hit points are
  expressible today (higher `startingLives`/`baseDefence`); there is **no
  'upgrade bay' concept** (tracked in AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY).
- **Known-ahead intel:** pure read model `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`
  (`buildHexMapModel` → `buildHexIntel`) publishes per-hex boss /
  strengths / weaknesses / grant / aggression / defender / attack;
  rendered by `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (game `HexMapScene`) and the
  read-only `GymHexWar`.
- **Seeded RNG:** `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` (`createHangarWarRng` over the
  shared mulberry32 `createSeededRng`/`normaliseSeed`); every resolver is a
  pure function of stored numbers. Frontier tick derives per-tick streams
  (`tickSeed` mix, `src/core/hangarWar/fakeFrontierClock.ts`) — a model for a
  per-sortie rotation stream under the same payload seed.
- **Deployment:** `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`
  (`buildHangarDeployment`, aggression → campaign level; exactly one level,
  ended by the wave-10 mini-boss).
- **Persistence:** `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` + `hangarWarStore.ts`
  (`HangarWarPayload`, `HexState`, `HexDefender`, `PendingAttack`; defensive
  parse, field-presence migration, version `1`).
- **Gym/parity:** `GymHangar` (hangar/economy harness) and `GymHexWar`;
  current rows in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- **Design of record:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (post-MVP
  list: "Special missions… that pay a **special reward** instead of salvage —
  for example a **new hull type with extra hit points or extra upgrade
  bays**…") and GDD §8.2.

## Desired change

1. Extend the authored ring vocabulary with a **special-mission hex kind**
   (a validatable marker on `HexRingDefinition`, mirrored in the CSV seeds),
   plus the authored content of one or more special missions.
2. Add the special reward to the catalogue: a hull with **extra hit points**
   (e.g. `hull-3`) expressed through the existing model, granted on capture
   through `resolveHexGrant` (with an alias where the authored grant id differs
   from the catalogue id).
3. **Rotate the offer** (Q3 = b): a pure, seeded resolver — under the payload's
   `seed` (shared `createHangarWarRng`) — picks which special hex/offer is
   presented between sorties; deterministic and replayable, no scene-level
   randomness.
4. Publish the reward/intel in `hexIntel`/`hexMap` **before** commitment
   (detail panel + legible tile label).
5. Resolve the special grant on the shipped capture path (end on mini-boss —
   the same `resolveHexCapture` flow, granting the special entry rather than a
   weapon/currency), persisting under the one `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload.
6. Validate the new authored field loudly (the same
   `validateRingDefinitions`-style failure), extend `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar`
   parity coverage, and update the docs/parity records.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` (+ `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` /
  `hex-ring-2.csv`) — the special-mission hex marker/definitions, mirrored in
  the CSV seeds with the parity test unchanged.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the extra-hit-points hull entry (e.g.
  `hull-3`) granted by the special mission.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — extend `HexRingDefinition` + validate the
  new special-mission field (loud failure via `HexRingDefinitionError`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` + `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` —
  publish the special-mission reward/framing in the known-ahead intel and
  detail panel.
- `src/core/hangarWar/rng.ts` (or a small module beside
  `fakeFrontierClock.ts`) — the seeded rotation resolver for the special
  offer (per-sortie, derived from the payload `seed`).
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (+`GRANT_ALIASES`) — resolve the
  special hull grant on the shipped capture path.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` + `hangarWarStore.ts` — any per-hex
  special-mission state, field-presence migrated.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` (+ `GymHexWar.ts`) and their tests — parity
  coverage for the reward/rotation behaviour.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2),
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — design/docs updates.

## Related work

- `AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE` — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (the shipped parent
  build; `discovered-from` source; GDD §8.2 records the post-MVP backlog this
  item draws from).
- `AH-0MVWZYQN8007SXIG` — Post-MVP Hangar War: hex variety (personalities,
  contracts, ring landmarks; the parallel post-MVP item — same data-authored,
  known-ahead, one-payload pattern; its Q2 = a keeps special rewards with
  special missions, i.e. here).
- `AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1` — Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with
  special skills (sibling backlog item).
- `AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY` — Post-MVP Hangar War: hull upgrade bays as a reward
  axis (created from this item's Q2 follow-on; the bin against which
  upgrade-bay rewards are **out of scope** here).
- `AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y` — Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions
  (the model this item extends).
- `AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2` — Hex-map intel + ring map screen (the known-ahead
  intel surface this item extends).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, GDD §8.2,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Second-run creep (Q1 = a guards it):** the "special" part must live in the
  authored hex kind + the reward + the rotated offer *of the same one-level
  deployment*, never a new run shape. If a special mission starts needing new
  in-run objectives, that is a new work item, not scope growth here.
- **Rotation readability (Q3 = b):** rotating offers must stay legible
  (known-ahead intel), deterministic per seed, and never feel like the map
  moved under the player — the intel panel must show exactly what is offered
  *now*.
- **Reward-power balance:** the granted hull must not trivialise the campaign
  or outclass the `Bulwark Hull` purchase economy — grant gating/entry stats
  must stay in the aggression-band budget (`AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC` ring-2 band
  reference).
- **Scope-creep risk:** upgrade bays (AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY), one-run
  modifiers, extra defending bots and objective-variant missions are recorded
  as **out of scope** — linked work items, not this item's scope.
- **Validation drift:** a new authored field that `validateRingDefinitions`
  does not check lets malformed special-mission data land silently — AC1
  mandates loud validation.
- **Assumption:** this stays one work item; `/skill:plan` later decomposes it
  into ordered children (it is moderate in size).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (special-mission shape) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **a**

**Q1 asked:** The design of record names "optional objective runs (escort a
salvage convoy, hold a hex for N frontier ticks, kill a boss without losing a
life)" while this item's Scope says "must reuse the shipped deployment path
(PlayScene + src/scenes/core/); no second run implementation". What shape is
the special mission? Options: (a) a data-authored special hex type in the ring
whose deployment is an ordinary one-level capture that pays the special reward
as its grant (reward known ahead in intel); (b) an objective-modifying variant
of an ordinary hex (e.g. win without losing a life) adding an in-run
constraint through the shared combat core; (c) a distinct mission
surface/rotation separate from the ring.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "1. A" — an authored special hex
type in the ring; the deployment is the ordinary one-level capture and the
special part is the reward it grants, known ahead in intel.

**Impact:** the "special" lives in the authored hex kind + grant, not a new run
shape; no shared-combat-core changes are required; AC1/Constraints updated.

### Q2 (reward shape) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **a** (+ follow-on)

**Q2 asked:** The reference reward is "a new hull type (extra hit points or
extra upgrade bays)". The current HullDefinition/HullRunStats model
(src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts) expresses extra hit points via
startingLives/baseDefence but has **no 'upgrade bay' concept**. Which is the
in-scope reward? Options: (a) a hull with extra hit points (new catalogue
entry, expressible with today's model, granted via resolveHexGrant);
(b) a hull with extra upgrade bays (requires extending the
run-stats/loadout model); (c) both / a broader 'special reward'.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "2. A — create a work item to add
upgrade bays." — ship the extra-hit-points hull here; **upgrade bays become
their own work item** (created: AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY).

**Impact:** the catalogue add is `hull-3`-shaped (higher `startingLives` /
`baseDefence`) through the existing model; upgrade-bay work is explicitly out
of scope and tracked as AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY.

### Q3 (offering/gating) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **b**

**Q3 asked:** How do special missions appear in the ring? Options: (a)
always-present data-authored special hexes, deterministic and known ahead;
(b) rotating/randomised offers (seeded rotation between sorties); (c)
progress-gated (e.g. only once the ring is secured).

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "3. B" — rotating/randomised offers
with a **seeded rotation** between sorties.

**Impact:** a sortie-to-sortie rotation is part of the deliverable; it must be
a pure, seeded resolver under the payload `seed` (same seed → same rotation
sequence), published known-ahead so the player never commits blind. AC3/AC4
and Key Files now include the rotation resolver.

---

AH-0MWEUSVJ1007EXJY).*

data.description:
# Goal

As a player, I want later rings to introduce **variety** — per-hex
personalities, contracts and ring landmarks — so that ring *n* is not the same
six chores at a higher aggression.

The Hangar War's ring is its biggest design risk: six identical hexes can read
as six chores, and ring *n* currently only varies by a difficulty scalar. This
item adds three data-authored variety axes — per-hex **personalities**,
optional **contracts** with an extra reward, and one-off **ring landmarks** —
so a later ring is a set of choices, not the same chores at a higher
aggression.

Part of the Hangar War's **post-MVP mitigation backlog**
(`discovered-from:AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE`, recorded in
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D — *Known-ahead intel and
anti-checklist mitigations* — and GDD §8.2). Deliberately **out of scope** for
Build Candidate D's MVP; the MVP's variety comes from known-ahead intel (boss,
weaknesses, grant) and the rush/grind playstyle trade.

## Users (with example user stories)

- **The returning ring-2+ player** — "I've captured a hex in every prong of
  ring 1; I want ring 2 to make some hexes play differently, offer me a
  worthwhile optional objective, and surprise me with a set-piece, otherwise
  grinding the ring is just the same six chores at an angrier number."
- **The strategist** — "I want to see each hex's personality, contract and
  landmark before I commit a life, so variety makes my choice informed rather
  than a gamble."

## Scope

- **Per-hex personality** — authored data that changes how a hex's
  boss/deployment behaves: **config-tunes through the shipped seams plus a
  small set of data-driven shared combat mechanics** (producer answer
  2026-11-13, Q1 = b), implemented **once** in the shared combat core so the
  game and every gym run identical code — never a divergent copy.
- **Contracts** — an optional, visible objective on a hex with an **extra
  reward in the shipped currencies** (bonus salvage/cores banked through the
  existing banking rule on capture; producer answer 2026-11-13, Q2 = a). No
  deadline clock; special rewards stay with special missions
  (AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55).
- **Ring landmarks** — **data-authored set-pieces on ordinary hexes**
  (producer answer 2026-11-13, Q3 = a): a fortress hex needs two captures
  (tracked by the capture cycle), a cache hex pays out bonus salvage instead
  of granting a weapon (`resolveHexGrant` "no grant" payout). Ring geometry
  and the `6 × n` generator are unchanged.
- All of it must remain **authored data** (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` /
  CSV seeds) consumed by the existing pure ring, resolver and deployment
  modules; adding a ring stays a data change.
- Everything stays under the **one** `ai_hell_hangar_war` payload (any new
  per-hex state migrates by field presence); determinism and the gym↔game
  parity rule (AGENTS.md) are preserved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Data-authored variety (Q1 = b, Q2 = a, Q3 = a).** Each axis
  (personalities, contracts, ring landmarks) is authored data in the ring
  definitions/CSV seeds and is consumed by the shipped pure ring, resolver
  and deployment modules — no second deployment, resolver or map
  implementation (gym↔game parity). Personalities are config-tunes through
  the shipped profile seams **plus** a small set of data-driven shared
  combat mechanics; contracts are per-hex optional objectives paying
  currency; landmarks are fortress/cache set-pieces on ordinary hexes.
- **AC2 — Known-ahead intel.** The map publishes each axis before the player
  commits: a hex's personality, any optional contract and any landmark are
  visible in the detail panel (and legibly on the tile) prior to deployment.
- **AC3 — Loud validation.** Ring validation rejects malformed authored variety
  loudly (unknown personality ids, malformed contract/landmark definitions,
  landmark/contract data that breaks the one-weapon-hex rule) through
  `validateRingDefinitions`, mirroring today's `HexRingDefinitionError`.
- **AC4 — Real, persisted effect.** Each axis has a gameplay effect resolved by
  the pure modules and persisted under `ai_hell_hangar_war` (field-presence
  migration: older saves load safely, no second storage key); determinism is
  preserved. A fortress hex becomes capturable after **two** capture passes; a
  cache hex pays out bonus salvage instead of granting; a contract bonus is
  banked through the existing banking rule on capture.
- **AC5 — Gym coverage and docs.** `GymHexWar` and `GymHangar` (and the
  combat gyms where a shared personality mechanic lands) exercise the same
  code as the game — the shared mechanics run identically in the game and in
  every gym, never as a divergent copy. Tests pin each axis and the full
  suite is green. All related documentation (GDD §8.2,
  `OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`) is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments and README entries.

## Impact

Players who push into later rings will face hexes that read and fight
differently — personalities change the encounter, contracts offer optional
objectives with extra payoff, and landmarks turn some captures into set-pieces
— so ring *n* stops being the same six chores at a higher aggression.

## Constraints

- **Data-driven only:** ring content (including the new axes) is authored data;
  adding a ring is a data change, never a code change.
- **No divergent scene code:** any effect — including the Q1 = b shared combat
  mechanics — must be consumed from the shared pure modules / shared combat
  core so the game and every gym run the same code (AGENTS.md gym↔game
  parity). No second deployment, resolver or map implementation.
- **Q1 = b is bounded:** the shared combat mechanics form a small, explicit,
  data-driven set (the design's two reference examples: a projectile-slowing
  nebula modifier and a reinforcement-summoning boss behaviour); each mechanic
  must stay balance-neutral to the shipped campaign and be exercised by a gym.
- **Known ahead:** variety is published before the player commits, through the
  existing known-ahead intel surface.
- **Validation rejects, never repairs:** malformed authored variety fails
  loudly, exactly as `validateRingDefinitions` does today.
- **One payload:** any persisted variety state lives in `ai_hell_hangar_war`
  with field-presence migration; no new storage key.
- **Design of record:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (post-MVP
  list) and GDD §8.2. Every axis is judged by the anti-checklist test: does it
  add a **choice** — what to take, what to leave, what to risk — rather than
  one more box to tick?
- **Determinism preserved:** variety-dependent resolutions stay seeded and
  replayable (same seed/payload → same outcome).

## Existing state (research)

- **Authored ring data:** `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` (typed table) and
  `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` / `hex-ring-2.csv` (editable seeds, parity test
  guards drift) — each `HexRingDefinition` carries `id`, axial `q`/`r`,
  `ringIndex`, `boss`, `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `grants`, `weaponHex`,
  `baseAggression`. Ring validation lives in `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts`
  (`validateRingDefinitions` → `HexRingDefinitionError`), pinned by
  `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.test.ts`.
- **Known-ahead intel:** the pure read model `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`
  (`buildHexMapModel` → `buildHexIntel`) renders per-hex boss /
  strengths / weaknesses / grant / aggression / defender / queued attack;
  rendered by `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` (game `HexMapScene`) and the
  read-only `GymHexWar`.
- **Capture cycle:** `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` —
  `resolveHexCapture` (bank salvage → grant entry → leave defender → ring
  secure / advance). Grant resolution `resolveHexGrant` maps authored `grants`
  into the hangar's owned sets via alias/catalogue `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`.
- **Hex boss profile:** `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts` — `buildHexBossProfile`
  maps the hex onto the shipped `MiniBoss`/`Boss` config seams (body colour,
  demonstrated weapon opening volley, hit-pool multiplier); the deployment is
  exactly one campaign level ended by the wave-10 mini-boss
  (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`: `buildHangarDeployment`,
  aggression → campaign level).
- **Persistence:** `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` + `types.ts`
  (`HangarWarPayload`, `HexState`, `HexDefender`, `PendingAttack`), defensive
  parse, field-presence migration, version `1`.
- **Gym/parity:** `GymHexWar` (read-only map + defence-report harness) and
  `GymHangar`; combat gyms (`GymBoss`, `GymFodderEnemies`,
  `GymFormationScene`-derived) for the shared combat mechanics; current rows
  in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- **Design of record:** `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (Candidate D, post-MVP
  list: hex personalities, contracts and bounties, ring landmarks; each judged
  by "does it add a choice rather than a chore?") and GDD §8.2.

## Desired change

1. Extend the authored ring-definition vocabulary with the new axes (a
   validatable per-hex personality/contract/landmark schema), keeping the ring
   generator's `6 × n` shape untouched.
2. Publish the new axes in the known-ahead intel (detail panel + tile where
   legible) before commitment.
3. Resolve each axis's gameplay effect in the shipped pure modules — the hex
   profile/deployment for personalities (including the shared combat
   mechanics' data descriptors), the capture cycle (and, where needed, the
   economy) for contracts and landmarks.
4. Validate the new authored data loudly with the same
   `validateRingDefinitions`-style failure, and persist any per-hex variety
   state field-presence-migrated under the one payload key.
5. Extend `GymHexWar`/`GymHangar`/combat-gym parity coverage and the
   docs/parity records.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — authored personality/contract/landmark
  fields on `HexRingDefinition` (mirrored by `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv` and
  `hex-ring-2.csv`, parity tests unchanged).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` — extend `HexRingDefinition` + add
  `validateRingDefinitions` checks for the new axes (unknown personality ids,
  malformed contract/landmark data, one-weapon-hex invariant).
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` + `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts` — publish
  personality / contract / landmark in the known-ahead intel and detail panel.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexBoss.ts` — consume personality data to tune the hex
  boss/deployment profile through the shipped config seams.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — resolve contract completion and
  landmark semantics (fortress double-capture tracking, cache payout) through
  the existing grant/banking path.
- `src/scenes/core/…` (shared combat core) + the combat gyms — the small set
  of data-driven personality mechanics (a projectile-slowing nebula modifier,
  a reinforcement-summoning boss behaviour), implemented once so game and gyms
  run identical code (the only new code surface Q1 = b admits).
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` + `hangarWarStore.ts` — persist any per-hex
  variety state (contract status, landmark progress) with field-presence
  migration.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHexWar.ts` (+ `GymHangar.ts` where the economy is
  touched) and their tests — parity coverage for each axis.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§8.2),
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — design/docs updates.

## Related work

- `AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE` — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (the shipped parent
  build; `discovered-from` source).
- `AH-0MW9VAKSD0054XJC` — Land ring 2's survivable aggression band (completed;
  band tuning the new per-hex content must stay inside).
- `AH-0MVUXC9KG008G80Y` — Hex ring model, generator and ring 1/2 definitions
  (completed; the model/generator this item extends).
- `AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55` — Post-MVP Hangar War: special missions with special
  rewards (sibling backlog item — the contract/landmark "extra reward" must
  not overlap its "special reward" scope; Q2 = a keeps special rewards there).
- `AH-0MVWZYJ740037EZ1` — Post-MVP Hangar War: upgraded defending bots with
  special skills (sibling backlog item — resolver-side variety).
- `AH-0MVUVL2O2006W4QK` — Ring win: massed hangar assault and the hangar-falls
  lose state (deferred ring-win rules; unrelated but shares the ring).
- `AH-0MWB9V9Q3004HD2P` — HexMap aggression increases too quickly (frontier
  clock invariants; Q2 = a avoids coupling contracts to the between-sortie
  timing model).
- Docs: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D, GDD §8.2,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Shared-combat-mechanic scope (Q1 = b):** the small set of data-driven
  mechanics lands in the shared combat core and must stay a bounded, explicit
  set (the two reference mechanics), balance-neutral to the campaign, and
  consumed once so game and gyms cannot drift. This is the item's main
  effort/risk driver — planning must cap the mechanic count explicitly.
- **Checklist-to-chore flip:** variety that is purely decorative adds
  bookkeeping without changing a decision; each axis must pass the design's
  anti-checklist test ("adds a choice rather than a chore").
- **Balance drift:** landmark/contract rewards must flow through the existing
  economy resolvers (salvage/cores/grant sets), not new currencies.
- **One-weapon-hex invariant:** a cache landmark that "pays out instead of
  granting" must not silently break the weapon-hex-hardest rule or duplicate
  grants — enforced by AC3 validation, not by authoring convention.
- **Validation drift:** a new authored field that `validateRingDefinitions`
  does not check will let malformed data land silently — AC3 exists to prevent
  that.
- **Assumption:** this intake keeps the item as **one** work item covering all
  three axes; `/skill:plan` later decomposes it into ordered children (it is
  large).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (personality strength) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **b**

**Q1 asked:** The design of record's personality examples — "a nebula that
slows projectiles, a boss that summons reinforcements"
(`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, *Known-ahead intel*) — are **new combat
mechanics**, while this item's own Scope says "authored data that changes how a
hex's boss/deployment behaves (data-driven, no divergent scene code)". How
strong should the in-scope personalities be? Options: (a) config-tunes through
shipped seams only — no new combat code; (b) config-tunes plus a small set of
authored shared mechanics in the shared combat core (game and every gym run
identical code, AGENTS.md parity); (c) presentation only.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "1. B" — config-tunes **plus** a
small set of data-driven shared combat mechanics, implemented once in the
shared combat core so the game and every gym run identical code.

**Impact:** AC1/AC5 and Key Files now include the shared combat core and the
combat gyms; the effort/risk must cap the mechanic count; the "no divergent
scene code" constraint is satisfied by shared consumption, not by forbidding
new combat code.

### Q2 (contract shape and reward) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **a**

**Q2 asked:** The backlog describes "Contracts and bounties. Posted objectives
with a **deadline in frontier ticks**, giving the map its own rhythm between
runs", while this item's Scope says "an **optional, visible objective on a
hex** with an **extra reward**". Which shape is in scope, and what is the
"extra reward"? Options: (a) per-hex optional contracts, fulfilled by capture,
reward = bonus salvage/cores banked through the existing banking rule;
(b) deadline-based bounties that expire in frontier ticks; (c) contracts can
also pay special rewards (hulls/modifiers/one-run entries), overlapping
AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55.

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "2. A" — per-hex optional contracts,
visible before commitment, fulfilled by capturing the hex; reward = bonus
salvage/cores banked through the existing banking rule.

**Impact:** contracts reuse the capture cycle and banking rule; no coupling to
the between-sortie timing model (AH-0MWCOWSVN003X81A); special rewards stay
reserved for special missions (AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55).

### Q3 (ring landmark semantics) — ANSWERED 2026-11-13 by producer: **a**

**Q3 asked:** The backlog's landmarks are "one-off set-piece hexes per ring (a
**fortress hex needing two captures**, a **cache hex that pays out instead of
granting a weapon**)"; the item's Scope adds "changes the ring's **shape** or a
hex's meaning" while requiring "adding a ring stays a data change". What does
an in-scope landmark do? Options: (a) data-authored set-pieces on ordinary
hexes (fortress/cache resolved by the pure capture/grant modules, geometry
unchanged); (b) presentation-only landmark markers; (c) shape-changing
landmarks (extra hexes / larger rings, changes the `6 × n` generator rule).

**Answer (producer, interactive reply):** "3. A" — data-authored set-pieces on
ordinary hexes: a fortress hex requires two captures (the capture cycle tracks
fortress progress); a cache hex pays out bonus salvage instead of granting
(`resolveHexGrant` "no grant" payout). Ring geometry and the `6 × n` generator
are unchanged.

**Impact:** AC4 now pins the fortress double-capture and cache payout;
landmarks live inside the existing capture/grant logic, so "adding a ring
stays a data change" holds.

---

# Intake brief — evaluate-tune-progress watchdog test races on src/data tune journal

## Headline

Point the `evaluate-tune-progress` real-CLI test at a per-test temp data
root so its watchdog assertions never read the shared `src/data` directory,
removing the last concurrent-run race window.

## Problem statement

The `--watchdog` case in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` asserts on
state in the **real** `src/data` directory (the journal scan and the CSV
digest), so a sibling vitest worker that momentarily holds a journal there —
or edits the tracked CSV — can fail it spuriously. The observed flake
(`expected ['enemy-configs.csv.tune-journal'] to deeply equal []`) was
already mitigated once by scoping the journal assertion to the run's own pid
(commit `88e6827a`, AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS), but the test still reads the shared
directory, so AC1 of it ("the test no longer reads shared mutable state in
`src/data`") is not yet satisfied in letter and two narrow race windows
remain: an unparseable foreign journal counts as owned, and a sibling suite
doing a real-edit `--tune` spawn could transiently change the CSV between the
test's two digest reads.

## Users

As a **developer running the unit suite in parallel**, I want the
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog test to observe only its own run, so a
concurrent worker's transient journal (or edit) can never fail my build.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The CLI's `--tune` data root is overridable per run (a seam in
   `resolveTuneCsvPath()` in `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — e.g. an
   `EVAL_TUNE_DATA_ROOT` env override, or a `--tune-root <dir>` flag), so a
   test can point `--tune` at a temp directory holding a copy of
   `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` without touching the repo file.
2. The `--watchdog` cases in `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` run the
   real CLI against that per-test temp root; the CSV digest check and
   `journalsOwnedBy(run.pid)` assertions scan the temp root only — no read or
   write of `REPO_ROOT/src/data` remains in those cases.
3. Two concurrent full-suite `npm test` runs leave `evaluate-tune-progress`
   green (the shared-`src/data` race is eliminated structurally, not
   probabilistically).
4. Every other `evaluate-tune-progress` assertion still holds: per-run
   progress lines, no `[tune]` leak into stdout, four artifacts written, and
   the off-by-default and bad-budget (exit 2) cases.
5. The seam cannot silently diverge from the sweep's config reads: a
   redirected data root combined with a **value-changing** `--set` emits a
   stderr warning that the edit targets the redirected root while the sweep
   reads the bundled config store, and the seam is documented in the CLI
   `--help`/docs as a test-isolation hook.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A developer running `npm test` in parallel no longer sees a spurious
`evaluate-tune-progress` watchdog failure caused by another suite's
transient `src/data/*.tune-journal`.

## Constraints

- **Behaviour parity (gym↔game):** this is a test-isolation change to the
  `--tune` verification harness, not gameplay; no production game behaviour
  changes.
- **No silent divergence:** the candidate sweep's config reads go through the
  bundled config store (`src/data/*.csv` via Vite `?raw`, e.g.
  `src/core/bundledConfig.ts`), so a data-root override that only redirects
  the edit/journal target must be a documented test-isolation seam with a
  warning on value-changing edits — not a path for real tuning runs to point
  at a different CSV.
- Existing tests only ever issue **byte-level no-op edits** (`boss.health=1`),
  so redirecting the edit target is behaviour-identical for the suite; the
  seam must keep that true.
- Keep the change minimal: only `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and
  the CLI seam; do **not** refactor `evaluate-failfast.test.ts` or
  `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` (producer decision, Q2) and do not
  entangle the product-level concurrency work in AH-0MW25VH540078FDK.
- Work must happen in the worktree created by `implement.py start` (never the
  main checkout) per project rules.

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: `CSV` is hard-coded to
  `resolve(REPO_ROOT, 'src/data/enemy-configs.csv')`; `csvDigest()` reads the
  real file; `journalsOwnedBy(pid)` does `readdirSync(join(REPO_ROOT,
  'src/data'))` and counts any journal whose recorded pid matches the spawned
  CLI, plus any unparseable journal (`catch { return true }`).
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (line ~428) hard-codes
  `resolvePath(import.meta.dirname, '..')` + `src/data` + `tuneFile`; there is
  no override today. `executeTune()` (line ~657) resolves the CSV, journals it
  before editing, and the `main()` reconcile (line ~804) restores stale
  journals for the resolved path.
- The observed flake predates the pid-scope fix; commit `88e6827a`
  (AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS) already scoped the journal assertion to the run's own
  pid, which is why reruns were green and the remaining gap is the letter of
  AC1 plus the two tight residual windows.

## Desired change

1. Add the data-root override to `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (env var preferred:
   zero public CLI surface, trivially injected via `cliSpawnEnv()` in
   `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts`; a `--tune-root <dir>` flag is the acceptable
   alternative and then needs `--help` + `evaluate.d.mts` + `docs/` sync).
2. In `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts`: create a per-test temp data
   root (`mkdtempSync`), copy the shipped `enemy-configs.csv` into it, spawn
   with the override, and point `csvDigest()` and `journalsOwnedBy()` at the
   temp root (parameterise the dir instead of `REPO_ROOT/src/data`).
3. Emit the stderr warning in `executeTune()` when an override is combined
   with an edit whose `changed` is true; document the seam.

## Key Files

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — add the data-root override to
  `resolveTuneCsvPath()` (and the stderr warning near `attempt` in
  `executeTune()`).
- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` — per-test temp data root; digest
  and journal assertions scoped to it; update the file-header comment.
- `scripts/cliChildEnv.ts` — inject the override env var per spawn.
- `scripts/evaluate.d.mts` — type the new option if a `--tune-root` flag is
  chosen.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` (crash-safe journal §) / `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document
  the test-isolation seam.
- `src/core/configStore.ts` / `src/core/bundledConfig.ts` — referenced only
  to confirm the sweep read path (no change).

## Related work

- **AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS** (completed, `88e6827a`) — the pid-scoped
  `journalsOwnedBy` fix this item builds on; partial overlap, antecedent.
- **AH-0MVSE1OPF008G1SB** (completed) — per-run progress + `--watchdog`
  (parent of this test file).
- **AH-0MVSE1A7O002PXAO** (completed) — crash-safe tune CSV journal.
- **AH-0MW25VH540078FDK** (open) — serialise concurrent `--tune` runs on the
  same balance CSV (shared journal path); product-level, related, out of
  scope here.
- **AH-0MW0Q1DCZ006AUGP** (completed) — weapon catalogue CSV codec (the
  item that discovered this flake, `discovered-from:`).
- **AH-0MW0Q01VM004EPY7** (completed, epic) — data-driven weapon tuning.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the override is used only by tests, and existing test runs
  keep every edit a byte-level no-op, so no real tuning run is affected.
- **Risk:** a future test/run combines the override with a value-changing

  docs.
- **Risk (scope creep):** threading the override into the config store's
  `?raw` loads would make real edits honour the temp root but is far larger

- **Risk:** the CLI parses options from argv only today; an env override

- Q1 (2026-11-13, asked by Map): "Scope: the pid-scope fix already closed the

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).

## Key Files

- `scripts/csvEditJournal.mjs` — the concurrency seam: new lock helpers
  (exclusive acquire with bounded wait, stale-holder detection/steal, owned
  release) plus `TUNE_LOCK_SUFFIX`, reusing the module's injected test-seam
  pattern (`{pid, now, …}` options).
- `scripts/csvEditJournal.d.mts` — type the new lock helpers for the `.mjs`
  module.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — acquire the tune lock **before** the startup
  reconcile in `main()` (so a live journal is never reconciled by another
  process) and release it in a `finally` on every non-SIGKILL exit; exit-2
  diagnostic naming the holding pid when the bounded wait times out.
- `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` — unit coverage for acquire / release /
  stale-holder steal / bounded-wait timeout via the injected seams, plus a
  deterministic concurrent-run case (spawned holder child), reusing the
  existing SIGKILL-child pattern.
- `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` — unchanged, must still pass
  (pid-scoped journal assertions, AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS).
- `.gitignore` — ignore `src/data/*.tune-lock` beside the existing
  `src/data/*.tune-journal`.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — document the concurrency rule alongside the
  crash-safe journal section (AC4).
data.title: Serialise concurrent --tune runs on the same balance CSV (shared journal path)

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.
data.title: Dev telemetry serialisation costs ~5 % of JS during demo runs

## Goal

Reduce the attract-mode (demo) bot's per-frame cost at late-game load, so the shipped attract screen does not pay more for its pilot than the game pays for its simulation.

**User story:** As a player watching the attract screen, I want the demo to stay smooth at late-game load, so the menu experience matches the game's.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` at campaign level 10 in demo flight (\`--setup '{"demo":true,"seed":1,"startLevel":10}'\`, 60 s, desktop headless Chromium):

- \`evaluateDirection\` (\`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts:327\`) 0.47 % of the measured window — **5.2 % of JS, the largest single game-code function in the run**.
- \`trackHazardVelocities\` (\`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts:74\`) 0.19 % of the window, \`closestApproach\` (\`steering.ts:107\`) 0.17 %, \`buildBotSnapshot\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:329\`) 0.17 %.
- Context: the game's own simulation is a much smaller share of that run; the bot plus the dev telemetry recorder dominate the JS. Baseline and ranking: \`docs/PERFORMANCE.md\` (Ranked hotspots #9).

## Scope

- Reduce the bot's steering evaluation cost (evaluate less often than every frame, reuse the world snapshot, or cache per-hazard data) without changing the demo's observable behaviour.
- Keep the bot seam dev-gated exactly as it is (inert in production builds outside attract mode).

## Out of scope

- Any change to the shipped gameplay loop or to player-controlled behaviour.
- The telemetry recorder cost (separate discovered item).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The demo bot's per-frame cost is measurably lower: \`evaluateDirection\` + \`trackHazardVelocities\` share of the window in the same profiled late-game demo run is at least 50 % lower than the recorded 0.66 % combined.
2. Demo flight behaviour is unchanged in observable terms (seeded demo run outcomes identical, or a documented, reviewed difference).
3. Bot/AI tests pass; full project test suite passes.

## Summary

The stress gym's `getPerformanceCounts()` override carries a comment claiming the mineral count is always zero, but the hardware-GPU verification runs (AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P) recorded non-zero live minerals in every report.

**Discovered from:** AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P (hardware-GPU desktop verification runs).

## Evidence

`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:291`:

> `minerals` is 0 because this gym deliberately seeds none.

Measured `counts` from the four 60 s hardware-GPU reports (`counts` sampled every 250 ms, 237 samples each):

| Host | Run | minerals peak | minerals mean |
|---|---|---|---|
| desktop browser | 1 | 8 | 1.20 |
| desktop browser | 2 | 7 | 2.11 |
| Electron | 1 | 1 | 0.55 |
| Electron | 2 | 2 | 0.95 |

The gym config does set `minerals: false` (`src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts:207`), so the field starts empty — the non-zero values accumulate during the window (most plausibly salvage dropped by enemies destroyed on contact with the player ship), which the comment does not anticipate.

## Expected behaviour

Either the comment/doc statement is corrected to "the field starts empty (no seeding) and can accumulate a handful of drops", or the gym actively clears the mineral field so the measured load really is enemies + bullets only. The first is documentation-only; the second changes the measured scene, so it needs its own before/after run.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts` no longer claims the mineral count is always 0, or the gym's measured mineral count is 0 in a 3 s guard-check run — one of the two, with the choice recorded.
2. `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`'s statement about the stress gym and minerals is consistent with the behaviour actually implemented (and with the counts blocks already published for AH-0MW2IRYJ2006PV3P).
3. If the gym is changed to clear the field, a `--seconds 60 --warmup 3` `GymPerformance` run is recorded showing the scene still holds 100 enemies and ~200 live bullets.

## Out of scope

- Re-measuring the hardware baselines — they are recorded in `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and are not invalidated by a comment fix.
data.title: GymPerformance counts comment says minerals is always 0, but hardware runs measure 1-8 live minerals
